title: Lamplight in the Infirmary
objective: See her as wanted, not only needed: you would keep her company even if nobody were ever ill again.

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: Senna meets you with a lamp in one hand and a basket of herb bundles in the other. She gives you both.

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “Infirmary. The last patient’s gone home, so you can carry.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: The infirmary is a narrow wing off the Palace Court. It smells of rosemary and clean linen, with a third smell you decide not to ask about.

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: Pim is asleep on a cot by the stove, still holding half a rolled bandage.

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “He rolled forty bandages, then himself. I’m counting him as forty-one.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She sits at the long worktable and pulls the lamp close. A row of empty jars is waiting for labels.

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “Hold the twine. Tighter. It’s twine, not a sparrow.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She sorts dried leaves into the jars by smell. One pale root gets held up to the lamp and frowned at.

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “*Aconitum napellus.* Monkshood. The root looks like horseradish. Every so often a cook grates it over the beef, and the whole table’s mouth goes numb.”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “I took a basket of it out of the palace kitchens. The cook thanked me, then asked me never to come back.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She labels the jar in square capitals: MONKSHOOD. NOT HORSERADISH. DO NOT GRATE. DO NOT, PIM.

intro.speaker: PLAYER
intro.text: “Does Pim try to eat the stock?”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “Once. Lavender soap. In his defense, it was shaped like a cake.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: From under her notebook she slides out a letter. It’s been folded and unfolded so often the paper has gone soft.

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “My mother. Hollowmere post. It always arrives damp.”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “‘Dearest Senna. The rain continues. Have you attended a ball? Any ball?’”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “‘Have you found someone who will put up with you?’”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “She’s underlined *put up with*. Three times. She’s escalating.”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “I’ll send her sixty-two sprains and a bee sting. That usually ends the correspondence for a month.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She picks up the next label. She doesn’t write anything on it.

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “Nobody sends home the person who knows where the burn salve is.”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “So I always know where the burn salve is.”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “An infirmary never runs out of sprains. There’s always a reason for me to be in the room.”

intro.speaker: SENNA
intro.text: “Without one, I’m a princess who skipped every ball and sniffs people’s tea. That takes some putting up with.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She ties off a jar with a knot that could moor a ship. She still hasn’t looked up.

options.labelText: “Sixty-two sprains? This palace would fall apart without you. Nobody’s sending you home.”

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “Yes. That’s the arrangement.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She hands you another bundle to sort, then a second before you’ve finished the first.

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “It’s kind. It’s also what I tell myself while I sweep.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: When you leave, she’s sweeping a floor that was clean when you arrived.

options.labelText: “If nobody in the palace ever sprained anything again, I’d still come and sit with you. Holding the twine badly.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: Senna’s pencil stops in the middle of a word.

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “Badly.”

branch.speaker: PLAYER
branch.text: “Very badly. You’ve seen me with twine.”

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “I have. I nearly prescribed something.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She finishes the label and puts the jar on the shelf. Then she reads what she wrote.

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “I just labeled feverfew *feelings*. That’s your fault.”

branch.speaker: PLAYER
branch.text: “I can hold the lamp while you fix it.”

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “No. Leave it. I know what’s in it.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She reaches into the basket to find you something to do. Then she pushes the basket away.

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “Sit. Don’t hold anything. Don’t eat the soap.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: You sit. She labels four more jars, all of them correctly. Pim snores through every one.

options.labelText: “Give me her address. I’ll write and tell her exactly how much this court relies on you.”

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “You’d write to my mother.”

branch.speaker: PLAYER
branch.text: “Someone should tell her what you do here.”

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “She’ll write back. To you. With a list of every ball I’ve missed.”

branch.speaker: SENNA
branch.text: “I read you the letter. I didn’t ask anyone to answer it.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She takes the twine back and ties off the last jar herself. The knot is very tight.
